Build a calendar-sample specification

Source: R/solve_by_sample.R
calendar_samples.Rd

Splits a calendar into samples for solve_by_sample() by drawing whole members of one level — seasons, weeks, days — and keeping every finer timeslice beneath them. The result is a plain table you can inspect, edit and pass back.

Usage

calendar_samples(
  calendar,
  level = NULL,
  sample_size = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  method = c("sequential", "random", "bootstrap"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

calendar

a calendar object.

level

character, the level whose members are drawn; the coarsest non-ANNUAL level by default (e.g. "SEASON" for s4_h24).

sample_size

integer, members of level per sample.

n

integer, number of samples.

method

one of "sequential", "random", "bootstrap".

seed

optional integer seed for the random methods.

Value

a calendar_samples data.frame with columns sample, timeslice and count.

Details

method chooses the traversal:

  • "sequential" — consecutive blocks of sample_size members in calendar order, tiling the year. Deterministic and full-coverage; the week-by-week or month-by-month crawl.

  • "random" — n disjoint draws of sample_size members (the year sampled without replacement); coverage may be partial.

  • "bootstrap" — n independent draws of sample_size members with replacement. A member drawn twice cannot be a repeated row (a calendar holds each timeslice once), so repeats are carried as a count and become a scaled share when the sample's calendar is built.

Samples are drawn as whole members of level. A hand-built selection need not be a complete cross: its calendar is irregular and keeps the full calendar's timeslice names. Each sample must keep at least two members at every non-ANNUAL level, so sample_size of 1 is refused for the coarsest level.

See also

solve_by_sample()

Examples

cal <- topia$modules$calendars$s4_h24

# two sequential blocks of timeslices, one row per (sample, timeslice)
sam <- calendar_samples(cal, n = 2, seed = 1)
sam
#> calendar_samples: 2 sample(s), method = sequential
#>   slices per sample: 48-48 | distinct slices used: 96
head(as.data.frame(sam), 3)
#>   sample timeslice count
#> 1    s01   WIN_h00     1
#> 2    s01   WIN_h01     1
#> 3    s01   WIN_h02     1

# two random samples of two seasons each, drawn without replacement
calendar_samples(cal, level = "SEASON", sample_size = 2, n = 2,
                 method = "random", seed = 42)
#> calendar_samples: 2 sample(s), method = random
#>   slices per sample: 48-48 | distinct slices used: 96
